threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 106 bus is a reliable option. Real locals know it’s just a suggestion for when you’re looking for a scenic detour.
On the 59 last night, a guy tried to sell me a weed cookie while reciting Shakespeare. Classic Brixton, where art meets the absurd.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? Watching a couple argue in Turkish over a döner while the tram screeched to a halt, blending chaos and culture.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find kebab shops that stay open past sunrise, where locals swap tales over midnight döner like it's a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re local when you can name at least three taco trucks that beat any upscale spot in the city, hands down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a bus driver stop mid-route to help a lost tourist with a map. Muni in chaos, yet moments like this remind you of the city's heart.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always expect late-night tapas spots to be buzzing, but most locals have dinner by 9. By midnight, it’s just us and the drunks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at how the bus schedules seem to change every day, standing there with a printed timetable in hand.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'overground' instead of just 'the train'—locals know it's just a hop to the Victoria Park for a pint.
Last night, the 59 was packed with a group trying to harmonize Adele's 'Someone Like You'. Half the bus joined in around Brixton station.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Passing the back entrance of Tempelhofer Feld, I spotted a group of kids BMXing with their own ramps. Just another afternoon of spontaneous joy, typical Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can find a spontaneous street performance by an opera singer at 3 AM. Only in Berlin will they belt arias while the rest of us are drunk on döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can spot the difference between fresh tacos at La Taqueria and those sad ones from a Stand. It’s a taste thing.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today with a lively street performer belting out classics. Riders were grinning, momentarily forgetting the delays looming ahead.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab a quick drink at any bar. But the locals know, post-8 PM, the best spots are packed with families enjoying their evening.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always look bewildered trying to navigate the winding streets and often end up stopping to take photos of the quirky buildings.
